subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic Gateway receive timestamp to agent-visible inbound metadata, and what canonical field name, timestamp format, and propagation boundary should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the field semantics would become a public cross-channel prompt/SDK contract that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define generic receive-time metadata
options.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests covering source timestamp versus Gateway receipt timestamp.

options.title: Keep timing in diagnostics only
options.body: Expose receive-to-dispatch timing through logs or diagnostics without adding agent-visible prompt metadata.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific traces
options.body: Let plugins add timing only where needed, accepting less consistent latency analysis across channels.

recommendation.title: Define generic receive-time metadata
recommendation.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests covering source timestamp versus Gateway receipt timestamp.

likelyOwner.reason: This is closest to the inbound metadata and message-received contract history tied to that handle.
